newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Chiron Corp expands management team.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Chiron Corp expands management team.

text.p: Chiron Corp said on Wednesday Edward Penhoet will step down as president and chief executive officer to focus on fostering better drug development polices to assist in the company's continued growth.
The change is part of an expansion of Chiron's senior management, in which Penhoet assumes the newly-created position of vice chairman. Chiron will recruit a new president and chief executive.

A joint founder of Chiron 16 years ago, Penhoet was instrumental in transforming biotechnology from a speculative research field to a profitable industry, while overseeing Chiron grow into the world's second largest biotech company.
Today Chiron is a $1.1 billion company that markets drugs for multiple sclerosis and kidney cancer among others, and has 25 new drugs, vaccines or diagnostic tools in development.

Penhoet said on Wednesday that the rapid growth in Chiron has required him to devote more time to government, industry and local communities over policy issues that are vital to its ability to develop and market new drugs. He said he hopes to foster better collaborative relations between research universities and industry and continue to advocate increased government funding for drug research.

Penhoet said that while the Food and Drug Administration has already made strides shortening and simplifying the drug approval process, changes are still needed to ease the burden on manufacturers seeking approvals.

As an example, he said modern diagnostic technology could be better used to speed the testing of new drug candidates. The so-called bDNA probe test Chiron recently developed, for instance, detects changes in viral load in a patient, offering researchers early signs of how well a drug is working, even before changes in the patient's overall condition are seen.

"The FDA has instituted some very positive changes, but they can go further," he said. "Biotechnology has become a major industry with more than $10 billion in sales a year and drugs that have helped millions of people."
He said he also hopes to shape public opinion "with respect to prevention as a major aspect of healthcare."

Among Chiron's five main business segments are two -- Chiron Diagnostics and Chiron Vaccine -- that focus on disease detection and prevention. Chiron markets a blood screening test for hepatitis C, and has vaccines in development for genital herpes and hepatitis C.
